thesis.objective: Determine and implement a secure managed-account gateway routing prerequisite for RC-011 without changing its acceptance criteria.
thesis.problem_frame: The current Elysia API uses one local cookie identity and Compose has one service; there is no account-to-container routing or gateway.
scope: Preconfigured two-account local proof gateway and isolated tenant APIs.
Server-bound sessions and tenant identity assertion across HTTP and WebSocket.
Executable isolation, failure, and browser proof before any RC-011 acceptance.
constraints: Do not trust client routing identity.
Preserve standalone local auth in explicit standalone mode; managed mode accepts only gateway assertions.
Keep gateway secrets outside tenants and agent/terminal environments.
Do not deploy, change credentials, or touch RC-002.
Preserve RC-011 original acceptance and failure conditions.
alternatives: Shared tenant network or Docker socket: rejected.
Gateway with fixed tenant mapping, tenant-specific assertion audiences, and isolated local proof networks: selected provisionally.
steps: Specify audience, auth mode, assertion transport, deadlines, socket revocation, user-visible failure, fixture cleanup, and telemetry contracts.
Implement gateway and tenant verifier only after the design gate is authorized and closed.
Prove two-account API and WebSocket routing and direct-port denial in isolated fixture.
success_criteria: Accounts A/B route only to their configured tenant.
Cross-tenant assertion and data access fail.
Internal ports are inaccessible from the relevant untrusted tenant/account networks.
Logout and expiry reject stale cookies and close proxied sockets.
Unavailable/stalled targets complete within a measurable bound and cancel upstream work.
test_strategy: Integration: real gateway and Elysia APIs for HTTP, WebSocket, revocation, timeout and cleanup.
E2E: Chromium A/B login, route/data isolation, logout/reload/error path.
Docker fixture verifies healthy control reachability before negative network tests and scoped cleanup.
rollout: Optional local proof Compose project only; preserve current default development Compose.
rollback: Remove optional fixture/gateway and retain standalone API mode; no migration planned.
observability: Structured redacted outcome with correlation ID, dependency category, status class and elapsed time; omit credentials, cookies, assertions, keys, hashes, and bodies.
residual_risks: Privileged Docker host is outside tenant network isolation.
Gateway compromise remains a multi-tenant trust risk.
RC-015 process isolation is distinct and RC-002 remains unknown.
Static mapping may not satisfy managed provisioning lifecycle.
recheck_triggers: Any requirement for dynamic provisioning or host-level isolation.
Changes to API auth/WebSocket, tenant topology, gateway replicas, or session storage.
Measured proxy deadline, socket closure, or resource cleanup outside explicit bounds.

verification.rationale: T-002 addresses design omissions but original internal-port proof remains conditional; reviewers identified missing numeric bounds and distinct UX details.
Direct-port boundary remains open; assertions, lifecycle and resource bounds are proposals only; replay and multi-gateway consistency risks surfaced.
Original direct-port criterion is not proven and mapping/session credential lifecycle remains a risk; do not present narrowed design as acceptance.

decision.rationale: Six blind reviewers identified material risks. Three fresh verifiers returned REVISE; the original internal-port threat boundary and measurable limits remain open, and no implementation evidence exists. Do not approve or accept RC-011.
conditions: Do not implement/publish this gateway design as accepted until design objections and original direct-port criterion are closed.
Do not change RC-002 status or retry/reconcile its prior provider effect.
change_summary: T-002 makes auth modes, tenant audiences, WebSocket identity transport, session revocation, bounded proxy behavior, fixture scope, telemetry and UX failures explicit.
Fresh verification found design still incomplete; no product change or RC-011 acceptance.
